text.en:
Sara noticed the school tap dripping all day. Her teacher measured: one drop each second made a full bucket in a day.
"So much wasted!" gasped Sara. She tightened the tap and told her class about it.

Fresh water is limited, so we must save it. Close taps, repair leaks, reuse water from washing vegetables for plants, and collect rainwater.
Soil is lost when wind and rain carry it away, especially where there are no plants. Roots of plants and trees hold soil together.
We save soil by planting trees and grass, by terrace farming on slopes and by not cutting forests. Using compost instead of too much chemicals keeps soil healthy.
Fresh water is limited. Close taps and repair leaks.
Collecting rain water is called rainwater harvesting.
Wind and rain can carry soil away. This is soil erosion.
Plants and trees hold soil with their roots. Planting more of them saves soil.

problem.en: How can a school save water?

text.en: Collect rain water from the roof.
Teach children to close taps. So saving small amounts adds up.

prompt.en: A friend says planting trees does not help soil. How will you explain?

requiredIdeas.en: Roots hold the soil in place.
Without plants wind and rain wash soil away.

points.en: Save water: close taps, fix leaks, harvest rain.
Soil erosion is soil carried away by wind or water.
Plants and terraces help to save soil.
